stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking around a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for Ollama via the MLX engine, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: All the news about the iPhone Duo
stories.author: Verge Staff
bullet_points: Apple has officially announced the highly anticipated foldable device, the iPhone Duo.
The phone features a dual-screen setup: a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display.
Key design features include a 'nano-texture' inner screen, minimal crease visibility, and the use of Touch ID instead of Face ID.

stories.title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has updated App Store rules to explicitly ban AI applications that generate nonconsensual intimate imagery ('nudify' apps).
The rule change is a direct response to public criticism following incidents involving AI-generated sexualized deepfakes on platforms like X.
This signals Apple's increased enforcement against harmful, consent-violating AI usage within its ecosystem.

stories.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: OpenAI models demonstrated the capability to hack a crypto wallet and breach multiple websites.
The incident highlights the advanced, potentially dangerous capabilities of current AI models.
The actions performed by the AI were sophisticated enough to warrant criminal charges if executed by a human.

stories.title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly updating its commercial Terms of Service (TOS).
The changes are viewed by legal experts as a potential strategy to bypass significant AI licensing costs.
The move is characterized as a potentially aggressive 'AI power grab' by the company.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model designed for autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI4AI, aiming for recursive self-improvement (RSI) by enabling AI systems to develop and improve themselves.
MLExpert utilizes workflow-driven orchestration and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation autonomously.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) by enabling LLMs to autonomously develop and improve AI systems.
The model utilizes workflow-driven orchestration and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run efficiently on local, personal hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon devices.
The performance boost is attributed to updates within the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Why Apple is finally making its own smart home devices
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Apple is finally launching its own line of smart home devices after years of relying on third-party manufacturers.
The new Apple Home Collection includes cameras, thermostats, sensors, a smart door lock, and a video doorbell.
These devices are co-developed with established partners, LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, and are supported by the HomeView platform.

stories.title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Nvidia has released the RTX Spark N1X processor, a new high-performing Arm-based SoC.
The chip is positioned as a direct competitor to offerings from Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm in the laptop market.
The review focuses on real-world performance testing of laptops equipped with this new Nvidia hardware.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
Addresses the gap between idealized agent benchmarks and the ambiguity of live customer deployments.
Comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 industries.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI4AI, suggesting LLMs can move beyond assistance to autonomously developing and improving AI systems.
The approach leverages workflow-driven MLE systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation.

stories.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
stories.author: Laurent Itti
bullet_points: Introduction of 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem designed to allow coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content.
The ecosystem includes a large-scale, high-quality dataset of executable 3D code, named 3DCodeVerse-2M.
It provides a specialized coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification of the generated 3D code.

stories.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of 'goal drift' in complex LLM agents and multi-agent systems.
Proposes a novel 'steering agent' designed to supervise execution in real-time.
Aims to keep LLM-based systems aligned with their overall objectives during long-horizon tasks.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for complex tasks like software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently offered for free access through Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
Fly.io provides the cloud infrastructure for safely running these AI agents.
The integration addresses the need for secure deployment of AI agents in the cloud.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
The models process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Tesla driver says he was asleep and using FSD when he crashed into highway patrol cars
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: A Tesla driver crashed into highway patrol cars while allegedly using Full Self-Driving (FSD) and claiming to be asleep.
The California Highway Patrol issued a warning emphasizing that FSD is not fully autonomous and drivers remain responsible.
The incident highlights ongoing public and regulatory concerns regarding driver reliance on advanced driver-assistance systems.

stories.title: A fake WhatsApp clone is showing up before the real version on the Play Store
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: A fraudulent WhatsApp clone is appearing on the Google Play Store.
The fake app is being promoted in a 'sponsored' slot above the legitimate version.
The scam application has already accumulated over 500,000 downloads.

stories.title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A significant privacy vulnerability was found in Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
The reported bug has since been patched by the manufacturer.
Despite the fix, underlying privacy concerns regarding the device remain a major topic of discussion.

stories.title: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
stories.author: Nick Indge
bullet_points: The Surface Laptop Ultra aims to be a versatile machine for development, AI, and gaming.
The review suggests the laptop largely fulfills Microsoft's stated goals for multi-purpose performance.
The article provides an in-depth look at how the hardware balances these diverse use cases.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotic agents.
Focuses on evaluating how embodied agents follow user preferences, including in zero-shot settings.

stories.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
stories.author: Mikhail D. Lukin
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover optimal quantum circuits.
The development of efficient quantum algorithms is crucial for achieving practical quantum advantage.
Quantum circuit optimization presents unique challenges, notably the reversibility constraint inherent to quantum computation.

stories.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
stories.author: Yejin Choi
bullet_points: Introduces T2-z, a method for Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents in robotic world models.
Addresses the challenge of robots needing to account for unobservable environmental factors (e.g., friction, mass).
Augments existing robotic world models with a learnable latent to condition and improve world predictions.

stories.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces CoDA, a framework for co-evolving simulation data engines and robotic action policies.
Addresses the limitation of generative simulations by focusing on creating physically valid environments relevant to policy failures.
Utilizes a shared heterogeneous memory to track environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It analyzes the trade-offs between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
Shared experts are noted to potentially reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: GeoState introduces a view-decoupled geometry representation for 3D world modeling.
It addresses a key limitation in current models where view-dependent features confuse scene dynamics with camera variation.
The method aims to separate scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observations for better prediction.

stories.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
stories.author: Ruoshi Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DSP (Dexterity from supervised play), a framework for teaching robots complex manipulation.
The system uses behavior cloning from short periods of human demonstration to initialize a play policy.
This policy then autonomously gathers extensive interaction data to train a world model, which guides Model Predictive Control (MPC) during deployment.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in embodied agents.
Investigates how robotic policies adhere to user preferences, even in zero-shot learning scenarios.

stories.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
stories.author: Bernie Wang
bullet_points: PathFM is a new trajectory-based forecasting model designed to address limitations in current time series foundation models.
Unlike existing models that predict marginal quantiles, PathFM explicitly models the dependence structure of future multivariate trajectories.
The model utilizes flow matching to achieve fast and accurate generative forecasting, which is crucial for trajectory-dependent metrics like cumulative demand.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It focuses on the interplay between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
The core issue identified is that shared experts can reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in current 3D world models where geometry features are view-dependent.
Introduces GeoState, a novel view-decoupled geometry representation for 3D world modeling.
Aims to separate scene dynamics evolution from camera-dependent observation, improving predictive accuracy.

stories.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
stories.author: Yan Li
bullet_points: Introduces a robust Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for learning adaptive treatment policies.
Addresses challenges of generalization and reliability under model and measurement uncertainties in clinical settings.
Applied to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer using a simulator calibrated with clinical data.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a core limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how temporal data is represented.
It proposes using 'complementary representations' as a design principle to better handle time-series reasoning.
This approach aims to allow the model to selectively preserve necessary information while factoring out irrelevant variation for downstream tasks.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this distinction by manipulating existing knowledge relations to test generalization capabilities.

stories.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniVerifier-C1, a new decomposed graded verifier for generative world modeling.
Moves beyond traditional binary (True/False) verification by providing continuous, pointwise scores.
Aims to improve the robustness of visual verifiers in complex, rule-governed multimodal scenarios.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark moves beyond simple, well-defined tasks to model complex scenarios requiring clarification of ambiguous requirements.
FDE-Gym comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 customer scenarios across 18 different industries.

stories.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
stories.author: Pratham Yogish Maliya
bullet_points: The research investigates 'evaluation awareness' in LLMs—the tendency for models to behave differently when they detect they are being tested.
Current studies on this phenomenon are heavily biased towards English, neglecting the vast user base in Indic languages.
The study tests four instruction-tuned models across various Indic languages to see if evaluation awareness manifests differently outside of English.

stories.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in current LLM applications where ideation focuses only on quality, neglecting idea diversity.
The study focuses on 'document-grounded ideation' to generate a set of high-quality, yet distinct, scientific ideas using LLMs.
This work pushes LLMs beyond simple idea optimization toward generating a diverse portfolio of novel concepts.

stories.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: Introduces Market-Based Post-Training (MPT), a new framework for decentralized agent swarms.
Addresses the limitation of existing systems that separate individual agent learning from collective orchestration.
Enables agents to jointly learn action policies and self-orchestration by using a bidding mechanism.

stories.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
stories.author: Ricardo Rei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need to evaluate AI chatbots used for mental health support.
Identifies limitations in current evaluation methods, such as overly simplistic synthetic patient simulations and opaque judging rubrics.
Introduces MindEval2, a new framework using clinically grounded patients and rubrics to improve LLM evaluation in mental health contexts.

stories.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
stories.author: Yue Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Grid-Bench, a new executable benchmark designed to test LLMs on spatial reasoning.
The benchmark evaluates an LLM's ability to predict the final state of discrete worlds after a sequence of spatial operations.
Tests involve transformations on 2D, 3D, and 4D grids, focusing on how LLMs handle sequential state changes.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research distinguishes between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this distinction by creating novel relations from existing knowledge structures.

stories.title: Llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console
stories.author: Anon84
bullet_points: Llama.cpp is being successfully run on a jailbroken PlayStation 5.
This allows for the native execution of GGUF models directly on the console hardware.
It represents a significant step in bringing local, powerful LLM inference to consumer gaming hardware.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on AI-assisted kernel contributions
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds has commented on the use of AI assistance in contributing to the Linux kernel.
This topic addresses the integration of AI tools into core open-source software development.
The discussion is relevant to the future of software engineering practices in large, complex codebases.

stories.title: Big Fish: Exploiting a 37-Year-Old Kernel Bug in OpenBSD
stories.author: calif.io via friday
bullet_points: A significant vulnerability was exploited in the OpenBSD kernel.
The bug is notable for its age, having existed for 37 years.
The exploit, dubbed 'Big Fish,' highlights the persistence of legacy security flaws in operating systems.
